title: From Scenes to Chapters: Creating Natural Flow
use_cases: Use when structuring a narrative to control pacing between slow reflective moments and high‑action sequences.
Implement when grouping related scenes under a single thematic umbrella to reinforce resonance.
Apply when signaling shifts in perspective, time, or location to avoid reader disorientation.
Configure when each chapter must feel like a complete unit yet hint at what follows.
Use when ending scenes with anticipation or unresolved tension to propel the reader into the next chapter.
content:
Chapters are assemblies of scenes, structured in a way that guides the reader through the story without disorientation. While a scene captures a moment, a chapter shapes how multiple moments relate to each other. Chapters provide rhythm, thematic unity, and breathing space, and can also be used to:

Establish pacing: longer chapters for slower, reflective moments; shorter chapters for action and tension.

Highlight thematic connections: scenes grouped under a chapter’s theme create resonance.

Signal shifts in perspective, time, or location.

Transitioning from scene to chapter requires attention to linkages. Each scene should end with a sense of anticipation, curiosity, or unresolved tension that naturally propels the reader into the next. Likewise, each chapter should feel like a complete unit, even as it points toward what follows.
